cultivar: Mixed large and small-leaf old trees
processing: Standard sheng: withered, pan-fired, rolled and sun-dried, then pressed or sold loose.
harvest_season: Spring is the prized picking as elsewhere; autumn pressings also exist.
appearance_dry: Mixed-size dark green leaf with some buds, smaller on average than in typical Banna large-leaf tea.
appearance_wet: Soft green leaves of mixed size.
taste_profile: A seller's note describes fruit and sugarcane sweetness with a savoury finish and a clear aroma; Yibang-area tea more generally is known for low bitterness and a fine broth.

brewing.notes: As with other Yibang-area tea, it takes gentle handling; there is little bitterness to tame, so focus on the aroma.

vintage_note: Sold by harvest year as single-village sheng, mostly spring, in small runs that may say Yibang or Yiwu on the label. One published spring list gave 2,200 to 2,400 yuan/kg, placing it among the higher-priced village teas.
description:
Malishu is a tea village close to Yibang town in the old tea mountains of Xishuangbanna. Yibang is known for its medium and small-leaf trees, and Malishu shares that mixed planting, which sets it apart from the big-leaf style most people expect from Yunnan.

The process is ordinary sheng. What matters is the leaf: one seller reports natural old trees of about 150 to 200 years, and a typical blend of large and small-leaf plants.

The documented tasting note is fruit and sugarcane with a savoury finish, smooth and aromatic. That is a single seller's voice, but it fits what is usually said of Yibang teas: gentle bitterness and a fine, sweet broth. Slightly cooler water than for heavy sheng suits this style.

Labelling varies. You may see it called Yibang or Yiwu area tea, so look for the village name and a stated year.
history: Malishu appears as one of the old tea tree sites of the Yibang area, alongside Mansong, Xikong, Jiabu and Mangong. Little is documented about the village's own history; its reputation has grown with the wider interest in single-village tea from the old mountains.
